About

Juan Cortés

I'm a junior at the University of Maryland, College Park, double-majoring in Mechanical Engineering and Physics. My research sits at the intersection of computational fluid dynamics, aerospace engineering, and applied mathematics — I'm currently working on fluid-structure interaction simulations of bat flight at the University of Tennessee Space Institute.

Beyond research, I co-lead the mechanical subteam of UMD's Accessible Prosthetics Initiative, where we're developing a myoelectric prosthetic hand. I also tutor undergraduate students in physics and engineering courses.

Long-term, I'm aiming for a career in defense and aerospace engineering, with a master's degree planned. I'm driven by curiosity — whether it's modeling turbulent flows, understanding quantum mechanics, or designing mechanisms that solve real problems.
